sections.h2: What rate does the city of Killeen charge?
sections.html:
Killeen's City Council adopted a property tax rate of 73.01 cents per $100 of taxable value for fiscal year 2027, which runs from October 1, 2026 through September 30, 2027. The city's budget announcement splits the rate into maintenance and operations and debt service.

City of Killeen adopted tax rate, fiscal year 2027, per $100 of taxable value
Part of the rateCents per $100
Maintenance and operations55.62
Debt service17.39
Total city rate73.01

For a median-valued Killeen homestead, the city estimated a city property tax bill of $1,699.83, up about $68.48 from fiscal year 2026, or $5.71 a month. The city notes that actual bills depend on each property's taxable value and exemptions. This is only the city's share. The full bill adds Bell County, the school system and any special district over your address.

The same announcement puts the city's total fiscal year 2027 spending budget at $316.36 million, with a general fund of $137.24 million. The council approved a 3 percent cost-of-living adjustment for employees and water and sewer rate changes effective October 1. Read the rate and the budget as separate things: the rate tells you what a taxpayer owes per $100 of value, and the budget tells you where the money goes.

sections.h2: Which office handles value and payment for a Killeen house?
sections.html:
The Tax Appraisal District of Bell County handles both jobs for Killeen, and the city's property tax page sends you to its site, bellcad.org. That site covers property search, exemptions, payment options and truth-in-taxation information. Killeen sits in Bell County, so a Bell County parcel number opens any bill question.

Payment options on the district site:

  • Online or by phone with a card or check, where the vendor charges a fee. An electronic check costs $0.50.
  • In person at any location by check, cash or money order with no fee.
  • After hours at the Belton office through the outside drop box.

The district also lists early payment discounts of 3 percent through October 31, 2 percent through November 30 and 1 percent through December 31, shifting to Monday when a date lands on a weekend. Confirm the schedule on its site each fall before you count on a discount.

sections.h2: When does Killeen property tax become late?
sections.html:
Tax left unpaid after January 31 goes delinquent on February 1, with a 6 percent penalty plus 1 percent interest that keeps rising into July. A collector that uses a private attorney can add up to 20 percent. The Bell CAD site also publishes its discount schedule, so paying in the fall can cost less than paying in January.

The January 1 lien explains why a payoff statement matters on a Killeen sale. Ask the district for the figure before closing, and ask whether this year's bill has been issued.

Help exists for an owner who is behind: a written penalty waiver request within 181 days of the delinquency date, four installments for seniors, disabled owners and disabled veterans on a homestead, and plans of up to 36 months where the collector offers them.

sections.h2: Which exemptions cut a Killeen tax bill?
sections.html:
Bell CAD says a homestead exemption is free to file, and it is the one most Killeen owners use. The district lists these qualifying exemptions:

  • Residence homestead
  • Disabled person
  • Age 65 or older, or a surviving spouse
  • 100 percent disabled veteran, or a surviving spouse
  • Surviving spouse of a service member killed in action
  • Surviving spouse of a first responder who died on duty
  • Donated residence of a partially disabled veteran, or a surviving spouse

The district asks for an updated driver's license or Texas ID, a Social Security Administration letter or A&B card for a disabled person, and a current or recent VA awards letter for a disabled veteran. It says no annual renewal is required, though the chief appraiser may ask for an updated application. Owners who file after April 30 are told to file anyway, and the district will provide any legislative remedy once the application is approved.

On top of the district's list sit the state school exemptions: $140,000 for a homestead and $60,000 more for seniors and disabled owners. A disabled veteran's exemption runs from $5,000 up to $12,000 by rating, and a veteran rated 100 percent can receive a total exemption on the homestead.

sections.h2: How does the homestead cap work in Killeen?
sections.html:
Tax Code 23.23 limits a homestead's appraised value to a 10 percent yearly rise, starting the January 1 after the exemption first applies. The Bell CAD page calls those 10 percent steps mandatory until assessed value catches up with market value. A long-held Killeen home may therefore be taxed on a value well under market.

The cap does not follow the owner to a new house, and it resets in the sense that a buyer's value is measured fresh after a sale. Protests matter too. A protest of value is generally due in mid-May. Homestead appraisal notices are mailed around April 1.

For a senior or disabled owner, school tax is frozen at the first qualifying year's amount, and the ceiling can move in proportion to a new Texas homestead. A city or county may adopt a similar limit, so ask what applies to your account.

sections.h2: What do the federal numbers say about Killeen?
sections.html:
Federal estimates put Killeen at 161,883 residents in mid-2025, up 5.7 percent over the 2020 base, spread over 54.85 square miles of land. Owners occupy 49.5 percent of homes, so about half the housing is rented. A typical owner-occupied home is valued at $215,400, and typical gross rent is $1,208. Middle household income is $60,977, and 23,452 residents are veterans.

The city calls itself a place with a military heritage, and it was founded in 1882. Veteran households make the disabled veteran exemptions above worth checking. The city's fiscal year 2027 capital plan includes $12 million for Stagecoach Road reconstruction, $3.1 million for Rancier Drive reconstruction and $610,000 for low-water crossing flood mitigation, which may interest a seller whose street is on the list.

faqs.q: What did Killeen adopt as its city rate?
faqs.a: The adopted fiscal year 2027 rate is 73.01 cents per $100 of taxable value, made up of 55.62 cents for maintenance and operations and 17.39 cents for debt service. County, school and special district rates are added on the same bill.

faqs.q: Who do I pay Killeen property tax to?
faqs.a: Pay through the Tax Appraisal District of Bell County, which lists online, phone and in-person options and a drop box at its Belton office. Confirm the account number on your bill first.

faqs.q: When is Killeen property tax delinquent?
faqs.a: February 1 is the first delinquent day for tax unpaid after January 31, and a penalty and interest start that day and keep growing into July.

faqs.q: Does Bell County give a discount for early payment?
faqs.a: Yes. The district lists a 3 percent discount through October 31, 2 percent through November 30 and 1 percent through December 31, and a weekend deadline moves to Monday.

faqs.q: Where is a Killeen homestead exemption filed?
faqs.a: File the free application with the Tax Appraisal District of Bell County. Bring a current driver's license or Texas ID, and add disability or VA paperwork if it applies. No yearly renewal is required.
